dedupe_keys.name: solar wind shocks and gicy indices for solar cycles 23 and 24 australian region

description: This dataset lists solar wind shocks from the Harvard Center for Astrophysics shock database for solar cycles 23 and 24 together with the ground response in the Australian region: for each shock it gives the time, the ground magnetic field change and GIC-index values for the x and y components, and the pre-shock, post-shock and step-change values of the interplanetary magnetic field components, solar wind velocity, density and dynamic pressure. The GIC index is a proxy for geomagnetically induced currents computed from geomagnetic field data. It was compiled by Richard Marshall and Michael Terkildsen of the Australian Bureau of Meteorology, Elizabeth Pearce of the Australian Space Agency and Colin Waters of the University of Newcastle, and underpins their 2022 Space Weather paper on forecasting GIC activity from solar wind shocks for the Australian region power network. It is accessible on Zenodo as one free CSV file (0.8 MB) under CC BY 4.0, with an earlier cycle 23 only version. Caveats: the GIC index is a proxy, not measured current in transformers, the data are regional to Australia, and shocks are limited to the CFA catalogue. It supports calibration of statistical forecasts and hazard exposure studies of geomagnetically induced currents in power grids; related records are INTERMAGNET and the major storm geoelectric simulations.
